title: ₹1,178.20 Crore Central Share Released to Karnataka Under Post-Matric Scholarship for SC Students During Last Three Financial Years
subtitle: ₹421.08 Crore Released in 2023-24, ₹422.90 Crore in 2024-25 and ₹334.22 Crore in 2025-26
body_text:
The Government has informed the Rajya Sabha that a total Central share of ₹ 1,178.20 crore was released to beneficiaries in Karnataka under the Centrally Sponsored Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for Scheduled Caste (SC) students during the last three financial years.
Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale shared these details in reply to Unstarred Question No. 2050 in the Rajya Sabha regarding Central funds for Scheduled Caste welfare in Karnataka.
The Central share released under the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SC students to beneficiaries in Karnataka was ₹ 421.08 crore in 2023-24, ₹ 422.90 crore in 2024-25 and ₹ 334.22 crore in 2025-26 , amounting to a total of ₹ 1,178.20 crore during the three financial years.
The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment implements the Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Castes (SCs) students as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme through State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. The scheme is being implemented through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode with effect from 2021-22.
Under the scheme, release of the Central share of scholarship is contingent upon the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations sharing the finally verified State/UT-paid data on the National Scholarship Portal. The scheme is open-ended and demand-driven for all eligible students of recognized institutions across India.
With regard to the Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes (DAPSC) , the Government stated that NITI Aayog issued guidelines in 2017 for earmarking funds under DAPSC. As per these guidelines, each obligated Ministry/Department allocates funds under DAPSC for the socio-economic development of Scheduled Castes through its respective schemes.
These schemes are implemented by the concerned Ministries/Departments, while allocation of funds to States and Union Territories, including Karnataka, is undertaken by the respective Ministries/Departments in accordance with the guidelines of their schemes. The funds allocated by obligated Ministries/Departments under DAPSC are reflected in Statement 10A of the Expenditure Profile of the Union Budget .
The Government's response highlights the implementation of scholarship support for eligible Scheduled Caste students in Karnataka through a demand-driven mechanism and Direct Benefit Transfer-based delivery system.

enrichment.summary: The Union Government informed the Rajya Sabha that ₹1,178.20 crore was released as Central share to Karnataka under the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SC students over the last three financial years: ₹421.08 crore (2023-24), ₹422.90 crore (2024-25) and ₹334.22 crore (2025-26). Minister of State Ramdas Athawale gave these details in reply to an Unstarred Question. The scheme is implemented via Direct Benefit Transfer since 2021-22, contingent on states uploading verified data on the National Scholarship Portal.
enrichment.context:
The Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SC students is a flagship Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment aimed at reducing dropout rates among SC students in higher education by covering tuition fees, maintenance allowances and other costs. Being demand-driven and open-ended, its funding fluctuates with the number of verified beneficiaries reported by states, and disbursement through DBT since 2021-22 was meant to curb leakages and delays that plagued the scheme earlier, when many states had accumulated pending dues. The scheme operates on a cost-sharing pattern between the Centre and states, with the Centre's share released only after states share finally verified payment data on the National Scholarship Portal, creating an incentive structure for timely and accurate reporting.

The reply also referenced the Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes (DAPSC), a mechanism instituted following NITI Aayog's 2017 guidelines requiring various 'obligated' ministries to earmark funds for SC welfare within their own schemes, distinct from the dedicated Special Central Assistance or Post-Matric Scholarship funds. This reflects the broader architecture of SC welfare financing in India, which combines targeted schemes (like Post-Matric Scholarship) with mainstreamed earmarking across ministries, monitored through Statement 10A of the Union Budget's Expenditure Profile — a document tracking allocations for SC welfare across the government.

prelims_questions.question: The Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for Scheduled Castes is implemented as a:
options: Central Sector Scheme funded entirely by the Union Government
Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented through State Governments/UTs
State-funded scheme with no Central assistance
Scheme administered directly by NITI Aayog
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states the scheme is implemented by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme through State Governments and Union Territory Administrations.

prelims_questions.question:
With reference to the Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes (DAPSC), consider the following statements:
1. It was instituted through guidelines issued by NITI Aayog in 2017.
2. Fund allocations under DAPSC by various ministries are reflected in Statement 10A of the Union Budget's Expenditure Profile.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release confirms NITI Aayog issued DAPSC guidelines in 2017 and that allocations under DAPSC are reflected in Statement 10A of the Union Budget's Expenditure Profile.
